hook: SCP-8980 looks like an ordinary file about a researcher whose computers keep turning against her, but you read it as an ethics investigator, with the original text marked up line by line. The annotations are the real article. It is long and deals with sustained workplace abuse, so give yourself time and some emotional room.
whyItMatters: It was written for a 2024 phobia-themed anthology and is a strong example of the modern wiki's interest in the Foundation's own staff as the source of horror. The color-coded review format, flagging what was omitted, misleading or never should have been written, turns the usual clinical voice into evidence against its author. The limits of the Ethics Committee and the institutional shrug at the end make it as much a story about bureaucracy as about one person.
thingsToNotice:
Watch how the annotations shift from pedantic style notes to something much heavier; the early nitpicks teach you to read the gaps, so you are ready when the gaps start to matter. Small recurring details, such as a supervisor's lateness, the pronouns used for her and a calendar that never arrives, carry more weight than any single scene.

The anomaly itself is pointedly petty, and the article quietly asks whether it was ever the main cause of her ruin. The final email shifts perspective once more, showing that the harm did not end when the case was closed.

related.note: Another staff member turned anomaly, treated with warmth and comedy instead.
An anomaly the file's author is said to have worked on, sharing its computer theme.
